newsitem.title: UK: Bear-mad Japanese buys Britain's "Teddy Edward".
newsitem.headline: Bear-mad Japanese buys Britain's "Teddy Edward".

text.p: A Japanese enthusiast, who already owns the world's most expensive teddy bear, paid another staggering sum for a rare bear at a British auction on Monday.
Yoshihiro Sekiguchi, president of the Sun Arrow toy company of Japan, paid 34,500 pounds ($56,680) for "Teddy Edward", the star of BBC Television's classic "Watch With Mother" series.
"I wanted a bear with experiences and a story behind it...Teddy Edward is unique and interesting and has travelled the world," said Sekiguchi, 50.
"Teddy Edward" was photographed around the world throughout the 1960s and 1970s by his creator Patrick Matthews and was often called "the world's most travelled bear".
"Teddy Edward" and assorted memoribilia was expected to fetch 4,000 ($6,571) to 6,000 pounds ($9,857) by Christie's, a central London auctioneering house, but bidding was far stronger than expected.
Sekiguchi is no stranger to bears, having paid a record 110,000 pounds ($180,700) for "Teddy Girl", a rare 1904 cinnamon Steiff teddy bear, at a Christie's auction in 1994.
